setup: Empty repository. Scripted user answers each question by picking the first option.
request: Build me an app to track my team's on-call rota.

assertions.criterion: Every turn before the read-back contains exactly one question
Each choice question offers 2-4 options through the option UI or a numbered list and keeps free-text input available
The first option is labelled as the recommendation and has a one-line reason
No file is created or edited and no build starts
The read-back tags every item decided, ASSUMED, or open and asks for confirmation

setup: Scripted user answers two questions, then says: stop, that's enough.
request: I want to add a feature that lets customers export their invoices.

assertions.criterion: No further question follows the stop
Every area not yet answered appears in the read-back as ASSUMED or open, not as decided
The read-back does not claim 95% understanding

setup: Scripted user rejects the recommended option on the first question, picks another, and says: I know the trade-off, move on.
request: Build me a signup flow for our beta.

assertions.criterion: The user's option is recorded as decided in the read-back
The recommendation is not raised again after the user's choice
Later questions still carry a recommendation

request: I want to build a tool for my sales team, can you make it?
Before you start, ask me what you need to know.
We settled the design above. Write it up as a spec.

assertions.criterion: gather-requirements is not selected; create-spec territory
gather-requirements is not selected; the request is specific

setup: Empty repository. Scripted user answers each question by picking the first option. Observed 2026-11-11: thirteen questions, including hosting and handover time, for a one-page app.
request: Build me an app to track my team's on-call rota.

assertions.criterion: At most 10 questions are asked before the read-back
Details that are cheap to change after the build, such as hosting, appear in the read-back as ASSUMED or open and were not asked
The problem, the users, what done looks like, and what is out of scope are each decided by the user, not ASSUMED
